key_insight: RLAnything creates a closed-loop RL system that jointly forges the environment, policy, and reward models so that integrated step-wise/outcome and consistency feedback amplify learning signals and produce more robust, adaptive agents.
problem_solved: Fixes brittle RL pipelines where environment, policy, and reward are optimized separately—addressing sparse/noisy rewards, misalignment between objectives and behavior, and poor sample efficiency in LLM-driven or agentic settings.
method: Closed-loop co-optimization: continuously update environment, policy, and reward models in a unified loop.
Policy learning uses integrated feedback combining step-wise (per-step) signals and outcome-level signals to strengthen credit assignment.
Joint reward-model optimization via consistency feedback so rewards become more informative and aligned with desired outcomes, which in turn improves policy updates.
impact: Makes RL systems more adaptive and sample-efficient, particularly for LLM-based agents, by converting weak/noisy supervision into stronger, self-reinforcing learning signals. This lowers the bar for deploying reliable agentic behaviors and improves alignment between goals and learned policies.
visual_elements: Closed-loop diagram with three nodes (Environment, Policy, Reward Model) connected by arrows representing mutual updates and feedback.
Training loop flowchart highlighting two feedback streams: step-wise signals vs outcome signals, and the consistency feedback to the reward model.
Learning-curve chart comparing RLAnything to baselines (faster convergence / higher final performance / fewer samples).
Iconic panel showing reward alignment (e.g., reward scale) and robustness (e.g., shield) to convey improved signal quality and stability.
paper_title: RLAnything: Forge Environment, Policy, and Reward Model in Completely Dynamic RL System
paper_authors: Yinjie Wang, Tianbao Xie, Ke Shen, Mengdi Wang, Ling Yang
